operations.comment: ; CNROM: fixed PRG CPU $8000..$FFFF, effective 8 KiB slots [0,1,2,3].
; CPU addresses below are execution aliases. Physical offset = CPU-$8000+16.
; Zero-page work bytes are heavily reused: pointer, decimal, sprite and sound
; algorithms describe their local register contracts. A symbol names storage,
; not a permanent type. Object and OAM arrays are separate CPU RAM pages.
; Object records use Y/flags/direction/X at offsets 0/1/2/3; larger objects
; reserve subsequent four-byte slots. OAM records are Y/tile/attribute/X.
; Attract bit 7, title bit 7 in mode_flags, pause bit 6, and bonus bits $30
; are interpreted by their individual consumers; shared bytes change roles.
; Static entry contracts do not establish natural execution. Unresolved game meanings
; remain tentative; every byte now has an independently accepted structural classification.
; Data: physical [0,16).
; Validated 16-byte iNES header: mapper 3 (CNROM), 32 KiB fixed PRG and 32 KiB CHR, vertical
; mirroring, no trainer/battery. Header is outside CPU address space.
; Data: physical [16,20).
; Four identity bytes $00/$01/$02/$03 used by the CNROM write helper for bus-conflict-safe CHR
; bank selection.
; Data: physical [20,272).
; Exact uniform $FF run. Prior boundary/reference inspection found no supported code entry.
; Retain generic non-code; padding or fill purpose is not established.
; Save the prior gameplay buttons. In attract mode consume duration/button pairs from the ROM
; script; otherwise poll both controllers and choose the active player. Live gameplay exchanges
; the low two bits; the attract script already supplies gameplay-format bytes.
; Latch both standard controllers, then rotate eight serial bits into their button bytes. Accept
; either of the low two port bits as asserted.
; Poll live input, select controller 1 or 2 using the player index, and exchange bits 0 and 1.
; Higher bits retain their serial-read order.
; Preserve the upper six buttons and exchange the low two button bits through scratch storage.
; Feed controller 2 through the same gameplay button normalization.
; Data: physical [379,395).
; Eight attract duration/button pairs read by ReadFrameInput. No local terminator or
; guard proves the full global selector domain; the following helper is an independent boundary.
; Fill nametable $2000 with tile $33 using the shared tile/attribute writer.
; No direct caller is known; this is a static entry contract, not observed execution.
; Select nametable $2800 for the same tile-$33 fill. Both nonzero loads branch unconditionally.
; Disable rendering and clear nametable $2000. The common writer emits 960 tile bytes, followed
; by 64 zero attribute bytes; the caller must arrange a safe PPU update window.
; Clear nametable $2400 using the same fill tile and attribute writer.
; A supplies the nametable high byte; fill_tile supplies the tile. The first three complete
; pages plus 192 bytes cover the visible tile area.
; With rendering disabled, upload 32 bytes of palette_shadow to PPU $3F00, reset the PPU address
; latch, then restore scrolling/control. Rendering is restored by the caller.
; Reset the scroll latch and write the horizontal/vertical scroll shadows, then PPUCTRL.
; PPUSTATUS reads reset the paired-write latch.
; Copy the 32-byte default ROM palette into palette_shadow in reverse index order.
; Data: physical [569,601).
; DefaultPalette: 32 NES color indices copied to the CPU palette shadow before the PPU upload.
; Advance the byte recurrence state = state*5+3 modulo 256. Increment once more when no gameplay
; button is held, making idle/input history affect later object choices.
; A is a zero-based case index. Pop the JSR return address into scratch_ptr; read a
; little-endian target from the table immediately after the call and jump without restoring that
; return address. Each target returns to the dispatcher caller.
; Erase the bonus countdown display, play the completion cue, update scores and leave through
; the common NMI epilogue.
; Update the bonus countdown every other frame. Convert it to packed decimal for the display,
; give periodic audio feedback, and continue updating the bonus sprites.
; During a bonus/transition NMI, render the decimal bonus value and optional two-by-two icon,
; animate/count bonus awards, then leave through the common frame epilogue. phase_timer
; distinguishes animation steps.
; Consume one remaining bonus item, add its score, refresh the decimal count and continue the NMI frame.
; Advance the bonus animation step and run common end-of-frame work.
; Use $FF as the completion handshake observed by the foreground bonus loop.
; At steps $24 and $28, reveal award icons according to the collected bonus counter. The exact
; icon meaning is tentative.
; Preserve A/X/Y, DMA the shadow OAM page $07, and select the shadowed CNROM CHR bank.
; mode_flags chooses title, bonus, paused or active-play work; all paths share the register
; restore/RTI.
; Refresh the scrolling tile rows and HUD, establish a fixed top-of-screen scroll interval,
; restore gameplay scroll, then update gameplay unless paused or a special event owns the frame.
; Refresh score tile shadows and sound, process Start/pause, rotate OAM ordering, increment the
; frame counter, then restore interrupted registers.
; Advance the shared frame counter on all NMI return paths, including title mode, then
; restore Y/X/A in reverse save order. IRQ points at the final RTI, so it does not consume an
; NMI register frame.
; IRQ vector lands directly on RTI. No IRQ-specific service is established.
; Update player-selection sprites/palette and live title input, then run sound before returning
; from NMI.
; Keep polling input and refreshing score/pause sprites; retain the gameplay state until Start resumes.
; Dispatch masked event_flags: death breakup ($04), stage-clear delay ($08), warp sequence
; ($10), or the remaining vehicle collision/fall animation.
; Update the four vehicle slots during an event frame without the normal spawn scheduler.
; Advance the player breakup animation, then continue vehicle event updates.
; Count down the stage-clear delay. At zero, set the negative event flag that the foreground
; loop uses to leave the stage.
; Advance the timed warp scene and refresh score tiles before the shared epilogue.
; Advance the warp timer once per eight frames.
; Drive a timer-based transition: initialize sprite visibility, animate scroll/rows, slow down
; selected intervals, and return to stage music after the final timer range. The foreground loop
; rebuilds the scene at timer $70/$90.
; Disable PPU output, rebuild palette/nametables and HUD/text, and mark the special display active.
; Choose a stage two or three positions ahead from the random bit, wrap six stages and advance
; the course counter on wrap. Rebuild the scene and convert remaining oil into score before
; restoring rendering.
; Data: physical [1421,1437).
; WarpScrollSteps: sixteen symmetric scroll step magnitudes indexed by the warp timer high nibble.
; Walk four-byte object/OAM records, preserve slots $40..$57 used by the player, and hide all
; other sprites while clearing their object flags.
; Increment the little-endian frame counter on the shared NMI return path, including title
; frames; carry into the high byte on wrap.
; Clear both scores and attract/player-selection/extra-life state for a new session.
; Copy the 32-byte stage/player defaults to active, player-1 and player-2 zero-page state banks.
; These are state snapshots, separate from controller bytes.
; Data: physical [1501,1541).
; DefaultPlayerState begins with the 32-byte state snapshot copied to active and both saved
; player banks. The eight following bytes remain generic data; their exact role is unresolved.
; Inspect one of sixteen 32-byte road strips per frame. A strip without unpainted tile $3D sets
; its bit; when both eight-bit masks reach $FF, enter the stage-clear delay and play its music.
; Set the completion bit for strips 8..15 and reuse the common all-strips test.
; Data: physical [1620,1621).
; First low byte of the sixteen road-strip pointers; the preceding BNE is always
; taken because it follows OR with a bounded one-hot mask.
; Data: physical [1621,1660).
; Remaining road-strip pointer bytes, then eight one-hot completion masks.
; Sixteen little-endian pointers select $0300+$20*n, n=0..15; masks begin at $8664.
; If bonus oil remains, consume one unit, add score, refresh packed-decimal count and play a
; cue. Otherwise advance the completion animation.
; Exchange 64 bytes at shadow OAM $0780 with the block selected by oam_rotation. Rotating sprite
; priority spreads hardware sprite-limit loss across object groups.
; Advance the selected 64-byte OAM block through $40/$80, wrapping before $C0, then exchange it
; with the priority block.
; Write the fixed WARP BONUS/OIL/1000 POINTS tile strings to three nametable locations; the byte
; ranges are split by screen placement.
; Data: physical [1813,1837).
; WarpBonusText: tile strings for WARP BONUS, OIL and 1000 POINTS. DrawWarpBonusText splits the
; 24-byte range across three screen positions.
; A selects a nametable column offset. Draw tiles $FC..$FF as a two-by-two icon, then clear the
; pending icon request.
; Clear both nametables, select CHR bank 3, load the title palette and copy a 1 KiB title nametable.
; Copy exactly four 256-byte pages from ROM $8AB8 into PPU $2000. The source pointer high byte
; advances at each Y wrap.
; Copy the title-specific 32-byte palette to the upload shadow.
; Data: physical [1976,2008).
; Exactly 32 title palette bytes copied to the palette shadow by LoadTitlePalette.
; Build four eight-sprite title rows, then write six copyright tiles at PPU $2349.
; The caller must provide a safe PPU window. No external caller is established.
; Initial carry can shift computed X coordinates; all RAM/table loop bounds remain fixed.
; Copy 32 title tile codes into four OAM rows and clear their attributes.
; Replace the bottom row X coordinates with eight explicit positions.
; Data: physical [2122,2154).
; 32 tile codes consumed by the title OAM initializer, one per sprite.
; Data: physical [2154,2162).
; Eight X coordinates for the bottom title row.
; Data: physical [2162,2168).
; Six tiles placed at PPU $2349; the codes spell the copyright year.
; Data: physical [2168,2175).
; Seven player announcement tiles copied by the accepted player message writers.
; Format player-one, high-score and player-two values and write six tiles to each
; of PPU $2083/$208D/$2097. No natural entry into this static helper chain is established.
; Write the six formatted tiles; the third score row falls through here.
; Convert the 16-bit value in scratch_ptr to packed decimal, emit four digits and
; two trailing zeroes, then blank at most four leading zeroes. Uses RAM $0200..$0205.
; Return the packed byte as high/low digit tiles in X/Y, preserving no A value.
; Clear title/gameplay mode state, discard the current caller return address, initialize player
; state and enter the foreground stage setup directly.
; Enable title NMI mode, wait for Start/Select, toggle one/two-player selection with Select, and
; enter attract mode when the shared high-frame counter reaches two. RunTitleFrame reaches
; IncrementFrameCounter through RestoreNmiRegisters, so title NMIs advance this timer too.
; With the high byte cleared, timeout is about 512 NMIs, depending on the low byte. Start discards the
; return frame and enters new-session setup.
; Move the title cursor tile between the one-player and two-player rows, blanking the unselected
; row, then restore scrolling.
; Detect a new Start press from raw controller history. In attract mode reset the stack and
; return to title; in play toggle pause, silence sound and resume the correct event music when
; unpausing.
; Restore the five-record pause sprite template; blink it off on alternate frames.
; Hide five pause sprites by replacing only their Y coordinates.
; Data: physical [2637,2657).
; OamTemplate: five four-byte Y/tile/attribute/X pause-sprite records. The preceding constant
; branch skips these bytes; DrawPauseSprites copies them in reverse byte order.
; A bounded 192-iteration scratch shift loop; used as a foreground delay, with no implied PPU
; timing guarantee.
; Save the active 32-byte player state, try the other player and inspect its signed lives byte.
; Return carry set if neither state has lives remaining; otherwise set player_index and carry
; clear.
; Copy active player state to the player-1 snapshot.
; Copy active player state to the player-2 snapshot.
; Copy the player-1 snapshot back to active player state.
; Copy the player-2 snapshot back to active player state.
; Data: physical [2760,2851).
; Zero-filled prefix of TitleNametable, the 1 KiB image copied by CopyTitleNametable. These are
; blank title tiles, not a CPU instruction stream.
; Data: physical [2851,3652).
; TitleNametable body: 32-byte tile rows with sparse nonzero artwork. The full 1 KiB copy starts
; in the preceding zero run and ends at the next supported code boundary.
; Data: physical [3652,3757).
; Zero-filled title-image tiles within the same 1 KiB TitleNametable copy; this exact uniform
; run is kept as its own baseline region.
; Data: physical [3757,3784).
; TitleNametable tail: remaining blank tiles and packed two-bit palette attributes. The next
; byte begins CopyTitleChoiceSprites.
; Choose one of two sentinel-terminated four-byte OAM record lists using the title player-choice
; flag. Preserve the first OAM record and copy from $0704 onward.
; Data: physical [3863,4049).
; TwoPlayerTitleSprites and OnePlayerTitleSprites contain four-byte Y/tile/attribute/X records.
; Each list ends at a leading $FF; CopyTitleChoiceSprites chooses by the one/two-player flag.
; Draw two length-prefixed tile strings at PPU $210A and $214A.
; A/Y supply the PPU high/low address and scratch_ptr points to [length, tiles...]. Write
; exactly length tile bytes; caller is responsible for a safe rendering interval.
; Data: physical [4105,4135).
; Two length-prefixed screen tile strings read by DrawBonusLabels. Each initial byte is a count;
; subsequent bytes are sent directly to PPUDATA.
; Initialize the player object at slot $40 and its jump/animation/input state. Object byte 0 is
; Y, byte 3 is X.
; Update the player motion/animation state, then expand the resulting frame into six hardware
; sprite records.
; Use road support and jump/landing flags to choose the car frame; a temporarily unsupported car
; follows the airborne state machine.
; Count down the jump timer, probe road support above, and choose ascent/descent frames. A
; detected intermediate road changes the jump phase and plays a cue.
; Use the player slot in X. Process road support and button-triggered jump state, paint
; supported road $3D to $3E, update travel scoring and select animation from signed travel
; speed.
; At low absolute speed reset the animation timer and index the direction-dependent turn/idle
; frame table.
; Save the gameplay buttons used for jump edge detection.
; During eligible animation phases accept a new normalized bit-1 jump request. Set jump
; flags/timer and play the jump cue; holding bit 4 selects the longer timer subject to player
; height.
; Advance the startup/turn animation timer and clear its button-edge latch.
; Discard the immediate helper return address and return a turn frame directly to the player
; update caller. This stack adjustment is intentional control flow.
; Read object Y, round to a four-pixel boundary and test the four road heights. Return zero on
; supported road tile $3D/$3E, $FF for a hole; other off-road cases return their comparison
; result.
; A supplies a test height while X retains the object slot. Select its road row pointer, map
; object X plus circular road offset into 128 columns, then test this and the adjacent
; travel-direction tile.
; Data: physical [4636,4676).
; SlowCarFramesOneDirection/OtherDirection select low-speed car animations. RoadBandPointers is
; four little-endian pointers used by road support and spawn-edge tests.
; A selects an eight-byte frame descriptor; X supplies the base object/OAM slot. Expand six
; offset positions with one shared attribute and six tile numbers, preserving X. Frames >=$20
; use the second descriptor page.
; Select the ROM descriptor page in sprite_frame_ptr according to frame index A.
; Data: physical [4784,5084).
; SixSpriteOffsets supplies six signed Y/X offset pairs. The following two car-frame pages hold
; eight-byte records with one attribute byte and six sprite tiles; the last byte is not read by
; the builder. Remaining bytes outside those referenced records have no stronger game meaning
; claimed.
; Update fire input, move both oil projectiles at slots $78/$7C, copy their positions to OAM,
; and clamp an underflowed oil count to zero.
; Require low turning speed, an unused projectile slot and a new normalized bit-0 press.
; Ordinary shots consume oil; stage-specific hidden conditions can arm special projectile
; directions.
; Check a fresh fire press, select projectile direction from player/jump state, and initialize
; it at the player position.
; Activate the projectile in X, copy the player position with a vertical offset, set its
; tile/attribute, consume one oil unit and count the shot for later special-object triggers.
; Move the projectile down two pixels per update.
; Only active projectiles move. Remove off-screen or road-intersecting shots; otherwise apply
; their direction bits to horizontal/vertical motion.
; Clear the object active flag and hide its Y coordinate.
; Copy object Y/X into its corresponding OAM record.
; Clear the player effect timer, select death event $04, silence current sound and start the
; death noise sequence.
; Advance the death timer every other frame. Apply phase-dependent signed XY deltas to the six
; player sprites; replace their tiles at timer $20 and signal life loss at $90.
; Data: physical [5534,5570).
; DeathSpriteDeltas: three groups of six signed Y/X delta pairs, one pair for each of the player
; car sprites in a death-animation phase.
; At sufficient absolute speed, increment the 16-bit travel counter every four frames and add
; one score unit every 64 frames.
; Use two slots $58/$5C on alternating circular road columns; attempt a spawn, move/check
; collection, then copy each position to OAM.
; Skip active slots. Use random state to choose a road height and probe the upcoming road edge;
; initialize a pickup at an edge X with the oil tile/attribute.
; Y chooses one of the four road heights. Select the screen edge using travel direction, then
; activate the object.
; Data: physical [5725,5729).
; RoadSpawnHeights: four road Y positions $40/$70/$A0/$D0, used by road pickup and hazard
; initialization.
; Move only an active pickup and test player overlap.
; Remove off-screen pickups. A player overlap plays a cue and increments oil up to 99; otherwise
; scroll the pickup relative to signed travel speed.
; Move object X according to signed travel speed, with a two-pixel correction above the speed
; threshold. Also used for floating score effects.
; Hide the object and its first sprite, then clear its active byte.
; Use the player at slot $40 as Y and test a small rectangular distance against slot X. Carry
; clear reports overlap.
; Y and X name object slots. Compare unsigned magnitude-like Y/X differences against 8 and 16
; pixels. Negative differences use ones complement, so the edge convention is asymmetric by one
; pixel.
; Y selects a road row pointer. Test two consecutive circular columns at the approaching screen
; edge for unpainted/painted road tiles.
; For object slot $B0, attempt a timed spawn, test movement/player collision and build its
; four-sprite picture. Probably the cat hazard; exact object identity remains tentative.
; An inactive slot becomes eligible after the lane dwell threshold or a periodic frame boundary.
; Probe the player road and initialize the four-sprite descriptor only on supported road.
; Choose the lane from the saved road selector and reuse pickup positioning, then copy four
; tile/attribute pairs.
; Y selects eight tile/attribute bytes. Populate four consecutive OAM records, preserving the
; base slot X.
; Data: physical [5985,6057).
; FourSpriteDescriptors: nine eight-byte records of four tile/attribute pairs. Shared objects
; choose records by an eight-byte index; individual visual identities are only tentatively
; known.
; While active, scroll the object with travel speed. On player overlap enter event $02, silence
; sound, move ordinary vehicles away and choose a direction-dependent event sprite descriptor.
; Move a hazard horizontally according to travel speed; its own Y is retained.
; Expand object Y/X into a two-by-two hardware sprite picture, centered with X offsets -4/+4 and
; Y offsets 0/-8.
; Quantize player Y into four road bands; return Y as the word-table index 0,2,4,6.
; Move the four event sprites diagonally on alternate frames until off-screen, then signal life loss.
; Track player lane dwell, then spawn/update the two-sprite hazards at slots $30/$38.
; Require an inactive slot, sufficient lane dwell and supported road. Slots $30/$38 use opposite
; travel direction and different portions of the 128-frame cycle.
; Move the active hazard, kill the player on overlap, and build its two-sprite picture. A
; near-center jump crossing resets lane dwell and arms a later stage-specific reward.
; Spawn/move the periodic collectible at slot $C0 and build its four-sprite image. Collecting
; three advances the warp event; visual identity is probably a balloon.
; A special trigger can force a descriptor; otherwise spawn periodically, choose random
; height/direction and initialize the collectible.
; Scroll the collectible, add a slow intrinsic drift and collect it on player overlap. Award ten
; score units, increment the counter and start warp event $10 on the third collection.
; Hide the lower two sprite records, then share the two-sprite deactivation path.
; Hide the object and its first two OAM records and clear activation.
; Every other frame, scroll one pixel against the signed travel direction.
; Data: physical [6728,6732).
; CollectibleSpawnHeights: four Y positions $30/$60/$90/$C0 chosen with the low random bits.
; While not in the jump flag state, compare the current road band to the previous one. Reset the
; dwell timer on a band change; otherwise increment up to $80 every 16 frames.
; Require a particular completion-mask/oil-count/trigger combination and an inactive slot.
; Initialize the object at the top road and select its sprite descriptor; the exact bonus
; identity is unresolved.
; Scroll left with a slow vertical drift, apply travel-relative movement and build four sprites.
; On leaving the screen mark the object permanently consumed with $FF.
; Use slot $D0 for the special object spawn/movement pair.
; Select the slot-$D0 special-object behavior by stage: first-stage life reward, stage-2 special
; road object, or stage-5 patterned collectible. Other stages return immediately.
; Spawn/move the first-stage reward and build its four-sprite picture.
; After ten oil shots, require a scroll-window condition, spawn the reward at the left edge and
; change the shot count to eleven to avoid retriggering.
; Move right on alternate frames. Player overlap increments lives and plays an award cue;
; leaving the screen deactivates the reward.
; Spawn/move the stage-5 collectible and build its four-sprite picture.
; Consume the crossing trigger, initialize the object at the right edge and clear its pattern
; index/countdown.
; Move left each frame while a ROM command sequence controls vertical motion and duration.
; Player overlap shares the collectible award path.
; Index two-byte pattern records with the object sequence index. Low nibble 1/2 means down
; one/two pixels; $F/$E means up one/two. Other nibbles leave Y unchanged; the second byte is
; the duration.
; Data: physical [7140,7160).
; CollectibleVerticalPattern is read as two-byte command/duration records, indexed by twice the
; object sequence index. The command low nibble chooses a signed vertical step. Unreferenced
; tail bytes and any intended termination rule remain unresolved; the earlier three-byte-pattern
; hypothesis is superseded by this consumer.
; Move one pixel at speed-dependent frame intervals, opposing travel direction. Low speed
; updates every eighth frame; higher speed every second frame.
; Reset scroll, load the stage palette and road layout, clear nametables, decompress the
; background, cache road templates, and initialize circular road/completion/trigger state.
; Apply speed/direction input, update hardware scroll and circular road column, then refresh
; collision road buffers and row-upload descriptors.
; Choose a frame-rate mask from absolute speed. On eligible frames increment/decrement the
; 16-bit horizontal scroll and reflect its low nametable bit in PPUCTRL.
; Add the pixel step in A to scroll_x/scroll_page; retain the page low bit as the horizontal
; nametable select.
; Subtract the pixel step in A and share the PPUCTRL nametable-bit update.
; Return $07 at low absolute speed, $01 otherwise: one pixel per eight frames versus one per two frames.
; Use normalized direction bits 7/6 to approach signed speed limits +$10/-$10. Jump-state
; constraints can suppress steering; update the matching direction flags.
; At sufficient speed and the appropriate four-pixel scroll boundary, advance or decrement the
; circular 128-column road index.
; Each stage has a 16-byte palette record: its first byte is copied to four sprite subpalette
; backgrounds, followed by fifteen background colors.
; Data: physical [7538,7634).
; StagePaletteRecords: six 16-byte palettes. A record gives one shared sprite background color
; and fifteen background palette entries.
; Increment scratch_ptr as a 16-bit little-endian pointer; preserves the source byte index Y.
; Increment the reused $13/$14 pair modulo 65536, preserving X/Y. This adjacent
; clone of IncrementScratchPointer has no established caller or natural execution.
; Apply a shared sprite background color, upload it and redraw HUD; set the special trigger
; latch and run a short delay.
; Disable rendering/control while updating. In a special display skip row work; otherwise
; alternate two of four road strips each frame, then redraw the HUD.
; Write preformatted score/travel/oil tile digits to fixed nametable locations and convert lives
; to one tile by adding $30.
; X selects a four-byte destination/source descriptor. Copy one 32-tile visible strip from a
; 128-byte circular RAM row, splitting at a nametable edge and toggling between $20xx/$24xx as
; needed.
; Rebuild all four row destination/source descriptors from ROM constants and current pixel/page scroll.
; Copy one four-byte template, add ceil(scroll_x/8) modulo 32 to its tile address, and choose
; the horizontal nametable using scroll_page bit 0.
; Data: physical [8017,8033).
; RoadUploadTemplates: four records of PPU low/high address and RAM source low/high. Current
; scroll modifies the PPU destination.
; Read eight 32-byte PPU strips into RAM template buffers, discarding each initial buffered
; PPUDATA read. The four-byte ROM records hold PPU address and RAM destination.
; Data: physical [8091,8123).
; RoadCacheDescriptors: eight records of PPU low/high source and RAM low/high destination. Each
; drives a 32-tile buffered PPU read.
; Refresh the four circular road buffers from cached templates while preserving already
; unpainted/painted road markers.
; Load template and circular-row pointers from a four-byte record. Copy 33 visible columns with
; separate modulo-64 template and modulo-128 road indices; retain existing $3D/$3E tiles.
; Data: physical [8236,8252).
; RoadBufferDescriptors: four records of cached-template pointer and circular-road pointer. The
; updater preserves unpainted and painted road markers while refreshing other tiles.
; Increment the 16-bit output pointer in scratch_ptr2.
; Data: physical [8266,8318).
; RepeatedTileLookup maps low command nibbles to repeat tiles; StageChrVariants selects the
; binary CHR variant by stage. StandardHudLabels follows as a 29-tile screen string. The small
; remaining alignment byte has no additional meaning claimed.
; Select the stage CHR variant and write the two compressed nametable streams at $20C0/$24C0.
; Normal bytes are literal tiles; $4x reads a repeat count for tile lookup[x]; $30 terminates
; the stream.
; Read a literal or run command from scratch_ptr. Repeat counts are byte counters (zero wraps to
; 256 writes); Y stays zero while the 16-bit pointer advances.
; Draw the active player number and a 29-tile label string. CHR bank 2 uses an alternate string
; for the bonus screen.
; Data: physical [8506,8560).
; BonusHudLabels contains the alternate 29-tile string. StageNametablePointers follows with six
; four-byte records, each the two little-endian compressed stream pointers for a stage;
; intervening alignment remains generic data.
; Select a road stream using the course counter, folding later courses into an eight-entry
; repeating range. Two tile values precede alternating run counts; $FF ends either count phase.
; Expand into RAM starting at $0300.
; Convert the unsigned 16-bit scratch input by repeated subtraction of 10000,1000,100,10. The
; four low decimal digits are packed into decimal_low/decimal_high; the ten-thousands
; subtraction does not store a digit, so inputs are effectively reduced modulo 10000.
; A is an unsigned score increment (display units, with separate tile formatting). Suppress
; awards during attract mode, add to the selected 16-bit player score, check life thresholds,
; and update the high-score maximum.
; Clear both little-endian player scores and the temporary award amount; preserve the high score.
; Convert the active score, travel count and oil count into tile digits. Remove leading zeros
; within each field using blank tile $40.
; X is the destination field offset. Expand the two packed decimal bytes into four tile digits
; $30..$39, stored least significant first.
; X starts at the most significant field tile. Replace up to three leading zero tiles with blank
; tile $40, leaving at least one digit.
; Use two bits in life_award_flags to award one life after score >299 and another after >1000.
; Compare the active player score; award flags belong to the active player-state bank.
; Shift A right four places to extract its high nibble.
; Disable APU channels, clear the enable shadow and set all four stream cursors to the stopped
; sentinel $FF.
; Only update normal gameplay audio when attract_mode is zero. Title/event callers can enter the
; unconditional channel updater separately.
; Update four independent sound streams with X = channel index 0..3. channel_register_base is
; X*4 and selects APU register groups.
; Cursor 0 initializes stream headers; $FF stops. Otherwise count down duration, compute the
; two-byte event pointer, interpret control commands and play a note. Stream headers define
; mode, volume/control and sweep.
; Compute the 16-bit stream pointer = channel base + 2*cursor. Stream event records occupy two bytes.
; For mode $20 preserve the byte; other modes rotate the header bits into the high APU control
; positions. Entry carry participates in the rotate before masking.
; For pitched modes, the low nibble indexes a base timer word and the high nibble selects right
; shifts (octave). Noise mode accepts values below $10 directly. Values outside these ranges
